thread:
sara: Heads-up — we're seeing a spike in JSON parse drops on the embeddings route for customer ACME (>6% over last 15m). Alert fired at 1976543175. Samples attached in the ticket.
tia: ACK. Do we have trace IDs or sample payloads? Are these failures in response parsing (model output) or in our ingestion pipeline?
sara: Ingestion path. Specifically POST /v1/embeddings with `metadata` field that some clients send as a JSON string. Our parser rejects when it's double-encoded or contains trailing commas. Example bad payload (obfuscated):
```
{
  "input": "...",
  "metadata": "{\"user\": \"bob\",\"prefs\": [1,2,],}"
}
```
Responses from the runtime: `400 parse_error: invalid JSON in metadata`. We currently drop and increment parse_drop counter.
mike: Noted. Eng-oncall bot shows alert group `parse_drop_rate` for `embeddings` with rule threshold=0.05. Can you paste a trace id from one of the failed requests? I want to look at the request/span logs across the router -> inference -> ingestion steps.
sara: One sample: trace_id=trc_0ff3c9a2. I pulled the router log and see `router: dropped payload due to json.parse` line but no redacted user identifier — good. But we can't see original metadata content (redacted).
eng-oncall-bot: Alert: parse_drop_rate (embeddings) — hosts: embed-node-7, embed-node-3 — 6.2% in 15m. Incident: INC-1976.
tia: Thanks. Two things: (1) we need better metrics to attribute to client library / SDK version (2) increase sampling of failed payloads for 1h so we can repro without full content retention. Any objections to storing full sample payloads temporarily in a secure bucket (auto-redact PIIs)?
alex: We should avoid storing raw PII. Proposal: store hashed user id + sanitized metadata with keys only (no values) for 1h, and store a tokenized version of the payload that can be requested by SOC under a support workflow.
mike: For immediate triage, can we add a dashboard panel: parse_drop_rate by `client_version`, `route`, `node` and show 500-sample payload ids. Also add a log correlation link that opens the trace with span filter `json.parse` so eng-runtime can inspect kernel-level failures.
sara: Repro steps I used: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KEY' -d @payload.json (attached). payload.json contains `metadata` as a quoted JSON string with trailing comma. It fails consistently on embed-node-3.
mike: Thanks. I'll create a short-term patch: make ingestion parser tolerant of trailing commas for `metadata` (config flag `allow_loose_json=true`) behind a feature flag for customers on enterprise. But we need product approval for changing default behavior.
tia: For observability: add a new metric `parse_error_class` with tags {route, node, client_version, error_kind} and make alerts fire on specific error_kind `double_encoded` or `trailing_comma`. Also add a Grafana panel and a PagerDuty runbook link.
sara: Action items:
- mike -> add dashboard panels + tracing link (due EOD)
- alex -> propose redaction + temporary bucket workflow (due tomorrow)
- tia -> add metric `parse_error_class` + alert tuning (due EOD)
- sara -> collect 50 failed sample ids and attach to INC-1976 (in progress)
mike: Pinged eng-runtime for escalation: @eng-runtime-team please review trace trc_0ff3c9a2 and advise whether this is parser config or model-side emission issue.
eng-oncall-bot: @eng-runtime-team escalated. Priority: high.
alex: Small note on privacy — make sure any stored sample goes through the sanitizer lambda that strips values for keys matching /(email|ssn|credit)/i before storage.
tia: One last ask: can support dashboards expose a small 'self-help' doc to customers describing how to format `metadata` properly (json vs string) and link to SDK helpers that auto-serialize? That should reduce future drops.
sara: Good idea. I'll draft a short KB and include a sample validator script. For now, monitoring + sampling + eng-runtime check is the path forward. Will update thread when we have root cause. :thumbsup:
